vray7max.label: V-Ray 7 for 3ds Max

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Sun parameters ▸ Enabled
entries.notes: Master on/off for the physical sun. off = no direct sun contribution (neutral off-state).

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Sun parameters ▸ Intensity multiplier
entries.notes: 1.0 = physical solar brightness; docs recommend keeping it and exposing via camera or color mapping. Values like 0.01-0.05 only when NO exposure control is used. UI accepts higher than 2 (practical range).

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Sun parameters ▸ Size multiplier
entries.notes: Visible sun-disc size AND shadow-edge softness; overall illumination strength stays the same (docs). 1.0 = real sun; docs examples use 4-40 for visibly soft shadows. Practical range; UI accepts higher.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Sun parameters ▸ Filter color
entries.notes: Tints the sun color (active as the tint in Filter mode, as the whole color in override mode). white = physical/untinted. Emit as a color instruction, e.g. 'warm amber for late-afternoon sun'.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Sun parameters ▸ Color mode
entries.notes: Options: Filter | Direct | Override. Filter tints the physical color, Direct/Override replace it. V-Ray 7's sun has NO Kelvin field — warmth comes from elevation + Turbidity + Ozone, or Direct/Override with a warm Filter color (docs).

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Sun parameters ▸ Color mode + Filter color
entries.notes: V-Ray 7's VRaySun has NO Kelvin spinner — Color mode options are filter | direct | override (docs) and sun color is physical (elevation + Turbidity + Ozone). To hit a target kelvin: lower the elevation / raise Turbidity for warmth, or set Color mode = direct with a warm Filter color; numeric kelvin white balance lives on the camera (cam.wb_kelvin). 5777 K = physical solar temperature, informational.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ move/rotate the sun head in the viewport, or Create panel ▸ Systems ▸ Daylight ▸ Sunlight = VRaySun ▸ Position (Date/Time/Location or Manual)
entries.notes: V-Ray 7 has no azimuth spinner on VRaySun itself — position is set by moving the sun or via a 3ds Max Daylight system with VRaySun as the sun type (docs). Compass: 0 = North, 90 = East. Emit as a placement instruction; default is informational.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ move the sun head height in the viewport, or Create panel ▸ Systems ▸ Daylight ▸ Sunlight = VRaySun ▸ Position (Date/Time/Location or Manual)
entries.notes: Elevation above horizon; sun and sky color follow the position physically — a lower sun is warmer with longer, softer-lit shadows (docs). Negative elevations reach twilight/dusk: the sun drops below the horizon and the PRG Clear Sky model keeps producing sky illumination down to about -12 deg (civil-to-nautical dusk), so a dusk reference is matched by placing the sun a few degrees under the horizon rather than clamping at 0. Emit as a placement instruction; default is informational.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Sky parameters ▸ Sky model
entries.notes: Options: Preetham et al. | CIE Clear | CIE Overcast | Hosek et al. | PRG Clear Sky (old) | PRG Clear Sky. For a fully overcast grey sky choose CIE Overcast. PRG Clear Sky is the modern physical model (twilight to -12 deg).

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Sky parameters ▸ Ground Albedo
entries.notes: Reflectivity/color of the virtual ground bounced back into the sky. gray = neutral default. A warm/green albedo subtly tints skylight fill. Emit as a color instruction when the reference ground clearly bounces color into the scene.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Sky parameters ▸ Indirect horiz illum
entries.notes: Intensity (in lux) of illumination on horizontal surfaces coming from the sky; scales overall skylight brightness. 25000 = default clear-day value. Practical range.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Sky parameters ▸ Blend angle
entries.notes: Angle (deg) over which the horizon blends into the sky, softening the horizon line. 0.1 = default sharp horizon. Raise for a hazier horizon transition.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Sky parameters ▸ Horizon offset
entries.notes: Lowers/raises the horizon line manually (deg). 0 = physical horizon. Use to hide a low horizon or tuck the sky behind geometry.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Sky parameters ▸ Turbidity
entries.notes: Air dust: 2 = clear blue sky/sun, 8+ = yellow-orange haze (docs examples 2-8). Affects sun AND sky color. Practical range; UI accepts higher. Default 2.5 confirmed from the UI capture (2026-07-03; pack previously assumed 3.0).

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Sky parameters ▸ Ozone
entries.notes: Ozone in the air (0-1): higher shifts the sun's light bluer, lower makes it more yellow/red. 0.35 = default. Works alongside Turbidity for sun/sky warmth.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Sky parameters ▸ Altitude
entries.notes: Observer altitude above sea level (m) for the PRG Clear Sky model; higher altitude thins the atmosphere. 0 = sea level. Subtle sky-color effect.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Sky parameters ▸ Night blueness
entries.notes: How blue the sky appears at night / very low sun (0-1). 0 = default. Raise for a bluer twilight/night sky.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Clouds ▸ Clouds on
entries.notes: Master on/off for V-Ray 7's procedural clouds (a section of the SUN — the VRaySky texture has no cloud params and follows the sun). off = clear sky (neutral). For fully overcast, prefer Sky model = CIE Overcast.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Clouds ▸ Ground shadows
entries.notes: off = one global lit/shadowed state decided at the camera position (fast, small scenes); on = precise per-point cloud shadows, slower but defined — for larger scenes (docs). NOTE: Vantage's same-named toggle means cloud shadows on/off instead.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Clouds ▸ Density
entries.notes: Density of the cumulus/stratus clouds: 1 fills up the sky (docs; examples 0/0.4/0.8). Default 0.5 confirmed from the UI capture.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Clouds ▸ Density multiplier
entries.notes: Multiplier on Density; larger values darken the sky at the horizon, 0 removes all clouds regardless of Density (docs). 1.0 = neutral multiplier. Practical range.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Clouds ▸ Variety
entries.notes: Variety of the cumulus/stratus cloud pattern (docs; examples 0/0.5/1). Default 0.3 confirmed from the UI capture.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Clouds ▸ Seed
entries.notes: Reseeds the cloud AND contrail pattern. RECIPE-CRITICAL: keep the SAME seed across attempts or the pattern changes while every other value matches — display-only, the model must not vary it.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Clouds ▸ Cirrus amount
entries.notes: Doc-stated scale: maximum 1 fills the sky with cirrus (high, wispy), 0 = cirrus gone. Default 0.2 confirmed from the UI capture.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Clouds ▸ Offset X (m)
entries.notes: Slides the whole cloud system along X (m). 0 = default. Use to move a cloud mass out of / into frame.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Clouds ▸ Offset Y (m)
entries.notes: Slides the whole cloud system along Y (m). 0 = default. Pairs with Offset X to reposition clouds.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Clouds ▸ Height (m)
entries.notes: Clouds position in height, meters (docs; examples 500/1000/1500). Default 1000 confirmed from the UI capture.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Clouds ▸ Thickness (m)
entries.notes: Lower = thin, sheer cumulus/stratus; higher = full and heavy (docs; examples 200/500/800). Default 300 confirmed from the UI capture.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Clouds ▸ Phase X (%)
entries.notes: Fine-tweaks the cumulus/stratus pattern along X and LOOPS at 0/100/200 (%). 0 = default. Small pattern nudge that keeps overall coverage.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Clouds ▸ Phase Y (%)
entries.notes: Fine-tweaks the cumulus/stratus pattern along Y and LOOPS at 0/100/200 (%). 0 = default. Pairs with Phase X.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Clouds ▸ Enable contrails
entries.notes: Adds aircraft contrails across the sky. off = none (neutral). Enable only when the reference clearly shows contrails; the sub-params below stay inactive until this is on.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Clouds ▸ Number of contrails
entries.notes: Count of contrails (docs: 5-40, spread randomly). Inactive until Enable contrails is on. Detail sub-param — display-only.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Clouds ▸ Contrails strength
entries.notes: Contrail opacity/age: lower = fainter/older (docs 0.1-1.0). Inactive until Enable contrails is on. Detail sub-param — display-only.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Clouds ▸ Contrails distortion
entries.notes: Wind-shear distortion of the contrail lines. Inactive until Enable contrails is on. Detail sub-param — display-only.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Clouds ▸ Contrails offset X (m)
entries.notes: Slides the contrail field along X (m). Inactive until Enable contrails is on. Detail sub-param — display-only.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Clouds ▸ Contrails offset Y (m)
entries.notes: Slides the contrail field along Y (m). Inactive until Enable contrails is on. Detail sub-param — display-only.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Clouds ▸ Contrails time
entries.notes: Animates contrail spread over time (docs animate 0-2). Inactive until Enable contrails is on. Detail sub-param — display-only.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Night sky ▸ Stars & Milky Way
entries.notes: Renders stars and the Milky Way in the night sky. off = default. Night-sky detail — display-only; the model matches daylight, not the star field.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Night sky ▸ Size multiplier
entries.notes: Scales star sizes. Night-sky detail — display-only.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Night sky ▸ Size difference
entries.notes: Variation in star sizes. Night-sky detail — display-only.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Night sky ▸ Brightness
entries.notes: Star brightness. Night-sky detail — display-only.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Night sky ▸ Intensity mult.
entries.notes: Overall night-sky intensity multiplier. Night-sky detail — display-only.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Night sky ▸ Latitude
entries.notes: Observer latitude for the star-field orientation. Night-sky detail — display-only.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Night sky ▸ Longitude
entries.notes: Observer longitude for the star-field orientation. Night-sky detail — display-only.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Night sky ▸ Milky Way mult.
entries.notes: Milky Way brightness multiplier. Night-sky detail — display-only.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Night sky ▸ Moon ▸ Size multiplier
entries.notes: Moon disc size. Night-sky Moon detail — display-only.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Night sky ▸ Moon ▸ Brightness
entries.notes: Moon brightness. Night-sky Moon detail — display-only.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Night sky ▸ Moon ▸ Intensity mult.
entries.notes: Moon intensity multiplier. Night-sky Moon detail — display-only.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Night sky ▸ Moon ▸ Glow mult.
entries.notes: Halo/glow around the moon. Night-sky Moon detail — display-only.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Night sky ▸ Moon ▸ Filter color
entries.notes: Tints the moon. Night-sky Moon detail — display-only.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Night sky ▸ Moon ▸ Azimuth
entries.notes: Moon compass position. Night-sky Moon detail — display-only.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Night sky ▸ Moon ▸ Elevation
entries.notes: Moon height above horizon. Night-sky Moon detail — display-only.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Night sky ▸ Moon ▸ Phase
entries.notes: Moon phase (new..full). Night-sky Moon detail — display-only.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Night sky ▸ Moon ▸ Rotation
entries.notes: Rotation of the moon texture. Night-sky Moon detail — display-only.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Options ▸ Invisible
entries.notes: Hides the sun disc from camera rays only; it still lights the scene. off = sun disc visible (neutral). Turn on to keep a bright sun out of frame while retaining its light.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Options ▸ Affect diffuse
entries.notes: Whether the sun contributes to diffuse shading (paired with a 1.0 amount spinner). on = default. Rarely turned off; folded amount default 1.0.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Options ▸ Affect specular
entries.notes: Whether the sun contributes specular highlights (paired with a 1.0 amount spinner). on = default. Folded amount default 1.0.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Options ▸ Affect atmos.
entries.notes: Whether the sun lights atmospheric effects/fog (paired with a 1.0 amount spinner). on = default. Has NO effect on VRayAerialPerspective (docs). Folded amount default 1.0.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Options ▸ Cast atmospheric shadows
entries.notes: Whether the sun casts shadows through atmospheric volumes (light shafts through fog). on = default.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Sampling ▸ Shadow bias
entries.notes: Offsets shadows to avoid self-shadowing artifacts. Sampling detail — display-only; the model must not touch it.

entries.ui_path: VRaySun ▸ Sampling ▸ Photon emit radius
entries.notes: Radius of the photon-emitting region (photon-mapping GI only). Sampling detail — display-only.

entries.ui_path: VRayLight ▸ General ▸ On
entries.notes: Master on/off for the area (plane) light. on = default. off removes the light.

entries.ui_path: VRayLight ▸ General ▸ Type
entries.notes: Options: Plane | Disc | Sphere | Dome | Mesh. Plane = default rectangular area light. Type changes which rollouts apply.

entries.ui_path: VRayLight ▸ General ▸ Length
entries.notes: Plane light length (scene units). With Units = Default (image) the SIZE also scales the effective intensity. 20 = default. Larger = softer light + shadows.

entries.ui_path: VRayLight ▸ General ▸ Width
entries.notes: Plane light width (scene units). With Units = Default (image) the SIZE also scales the effective intensity. 20 = default. Pairs with Length for the softbox size.

entries.ui_path: VRayLight ▸ General ▸ Units
entries.notes: Options: Default (image) | Luminous power (lm) | Luminance (lm/m²/sr) | Radiant power (W) | Radiance (W/m²/sr). Default (image) makes Multiplier size-dependent; photometric units make it size-independent.

entries.ui_path: VRayLight ▸ General ▸ Multiplier
entries.notes: Brightness of the plane/area light; with Units = Default (image) it also depends on the light's SIZE. Default 30.0 confirmed from the UI capture. Practical range; UI accepts higher. (The fill-workflow lever fill.plane_intensity targets this same control.)

entries.ui_path: VRayLight ▸ General ▸ Mode
entries.notes: Options: Color | Temperature. Color uses the color swatch; Temperature enables the Kelvin field below. Color = default.

entries.ui_path: VRayLight ▸ General ▸ Color
entries.notes: Light color (active when Mode = Color). white = neutral. Emit as a color instruction to warm/cool a fill.

entries.ui_path: VRayLight ▸ General ▸ Temperature (Mode = Temperature)
entries.notes: Kelvin color of the light; active only when Mode = Temperature. 6500 K = neutral daylight. Lower = warmer fill.

entries.ui_path: VRayLight ▸ General ▸ Map
entries.notes: Texture slot (with an on/off checkbox) projected by the light; a map overrides Color/Temperature. none = no texture. Value = texture file or mood description, not a number.

entries.ui_path: VRayLight ▸ Plane/disc light ▸ Directional
entries.notes: Focuses the plane light into a more directional beam (0 = full hemisphere spread, 1 = tight). 0 = default soft area light.

entries.ui_path: VRayLight ▸ Plane/disc light ▸ Directional strength
entries.notes: Strength of the directional focusing above. 0.9 = default. Interacts with Directional to shape falloff.

entries.ui_path: VRayLight ▸ Plane/disc light ▸ Preview
entries.notes: Options: Never | Always | Selected. Viewport preview of the directional shape — viewport display only, not a lighting value.

entries.ui_path: VRayLight ▸ Options ▸ Cast shadows
entries.notes: Whether the light casts shadows. on = default. Turn off for a pure fill that adds no shadowing.

entries.ui_path: VRayLight ▸ Options ▸ Double-sided
entries.notes: Emits from both faces of the plane instead of one. off = default (one-sided). Turn on to light from both sides.

entries.ui_path: VRayLight ▸ Options ▸ Invisible
entries.notes: Hides the light shape from camera rays; it still lights the scene. off = default (shape visible). Turn on to keep a fill out of frame.

entries.ui_path: VRayLight ▸ Options ▸ Affect diffuse
entries.notes: Whether the light contributes to diffuse shading (paired with a 1.0 amount spinner). on = default. Folded amount default 1.0.

entries.ui_path: VRayLight ▸ Options ▸ Affect specular
entries.notes: Whether the light contributes specular highlights (paired with a 1.0 amount spinner). on = default. Turn off to kill a fill's highlights. Folded amount default 1.0.

entries.ui_path: VRayLight ▸ Options ▸ Affect reflections
entries.notes: Whether the light shows up in reflections. on = default. Turn off so a fill does not appear as a reflected softbox.

entries.ui_path: VRayLight ▸ Options ▸ Affect atmos.
entries.notes: Whether the light lights atmospheric effects/fog (paired with a 1.0 amount spinner). on = default. Folded amount default 1.0.

entries.ui_path: VRayLight ▸ Sampling ▸ Shadow bias
entries.notes: Offsets shadows to avoid self-shadowing artifacts. Sampling detail — display-only.

entries.ui_path: VRayLight ▸ Sampling ▸ Tex resolution
entries.notes: Resolution used to sample a texture in the light's Map slot. Sampling detail — display-only.

entries.ui_path: VRayLight ▸ Decay ▸ Near on
entries.notes: Enables a near-attenuation start distance (non-physical falloff). off = default. Decay control — display-only.

entries.ui_path: VRayLight ▸ Decay ▸ Far on
entries.notes: Enables a far-attenuation end distance (non-physical falloff). off = default. Decay control — display-only.

entries.ui_path: VRayLight ▸ Viewport ▸ Viewport wire color
entries.notes: Viewport wireframe color of the light gizmo (with an on/off override checkbox, default off). Purely a viewport display cue — the model must NOT emit it.

entries.ui_path: VRayIES ▸ General ▸ Enabled
entries.notes: Master on/off for the IES photometric light. on = default. off removes it.

entries.ui_path: VRayIES ▸ General ▸ Targeted
entries.notes: Whether the IES light uses a target node to aim. on = default. Placement/aim behavior.

entries.ui_path: VRayIES ▸ General ▸ IES file
entries.notes: The .ies photometric profile file. none = unset. Value = IES file or fixture description; the profile shapes the beam.

entries.ui_path: VRayIES ▸ Intensity and color ▸ Intensity value
entries.notes: Luminous intensity (units per Intensity type). 1700 = default. Raise/lower to match fixture brightness.

entries.ui_path: VRayIES ▸ Intensity and color ▸ Intensity type
entries.notes: Options: power (lm) | candelas (cd) | ... — the unit that Intensity value is expressed in. power (lm) = default.

entries.ui_path: VRayIES ▸ Intensity and color ▸ Override intensity
entries.notes: Options: rescale | replace | none — how the Intensity value interacts with the value baked into the IES file. rescale = default.

entries.ui_path: VRayIES ▸ Intensity and color ▸ Color mode
entries.notes: Options: Color | Temperature. Color uses the swatch; Temperature enables the Kelvin field. Color = default.

entries.ui_path: VRayIES ▸ Intensity and color ▸ Color
entries.notes: IES light color (active when Color mode = Color). Capture shows magenta as the current value. Emit as a color instruction; set to a neutral/warm fixture tone to match.

entries.ui_path: VRayIES ▸ Intensity and color ▸ Color temperature
entries.notes: Kelvin color; active only when Color mode = Temperature. 6500 K = neutral daylight.

entries.ui_path: VRayIES ▸ Sampling ▸ Shadow bias
entries.notes: Offsets shadows to avoid self-shadowing. Sampling detail — display-only.

entries.ui_path: VRayIES ▸ Options ▸ Cast shadows
entries.notes: Whether the IES light casts shadows. on = default.

entries.ui_path: VRayIES ▸ Options ▸ Affect diffuse
entries.notes: Whether the IES light contributes diffuse (paired 1.0 amount). on = default.

entries.ui_path: VRayIES ▸ Options ▸ Affect specular
entries.notes: Whether the IES light contributes specular (paired 1.0 amount). on = default.

entries.ui_path: VRayIES ▸ Options ▸ Affect atmos.
entries.notes: Whether the IES light lights atmosphere/fog (paired 1.0 amount). on = default.

entries.ui_path: VRayIES ▸ Options ▸ Use light shape
entries.notes: Options: For shadow | Always | Never — whether the IES-defined shape is used for shadowing/illumination. For shadow = default.

entries.ui_path: VRayIES ▸ Viewport ▸ Show distribution
entries.notes: Draws the IES distribution web in the viewport. Viewport display only — the model must NOT emit it.

entries.ui_path: VRayIES ▸ IES override ▸ Override shape
entries.notes: Overrides the light's physical shape (adds inactive Shape/Height/Width/Length/Diameter fields). off = default (use the IES-defined shape). Shape-override detail — display-only.

entries.ui_path: VRayLuminaire ▸ General ▸ Enabled
entries.notes: Master on/off for the luminaire (packaged fixture). on = default.

entries.ui_path: VRayLuminaire ▸ General ▸ Luminaire file
entries.notes: The luminaire definition file. none = unset. Value = file or fixture description.

entries.ui_path: VRayLuminaire ▸ General ▸ Scale
entries.notes: Geometric scale of the luminaire. 1.0 = default. Larger physical fixture.

entries.ui_path: VRayLuminaire ▸ Intensity and color ▸ Intensity
entries.notes: Brightness multiplier of the luminaire. 1.0 = default. Raise/lower to match fixture output.

entries.ui_path: VRayLuminaire ▸ Intensity and color ▸ Color mode
entries.notes: Options: Color | Temperature. Color = default; Temperature enables the Kelvin field.

entries.ui_path: VRayLuminaire ▸ Intensity and color ▸ Color
entries.notes: Luminaire color (active when Color mode = Color). white = neutral. Emit as a color instruction.

entries.ui_path: VRayLuminaire ▸ Intensity and color ▸ Color temperature
entries.notes: Kelvin color; active only when Color mode = Temperature. 6500 K = neutral daylight (inactive at default).

entries.ui_path: VRayLuminaire ▸ Options ▸ Affect diffuse
entries.notes: Diffuse contribution amount of the luminaire. 1.0 = default (full).

entries.ui_path: VRayLuminaire ▸ Options ▸ Affect specular
entries.notes: Specular contribution amount of the luminaire. 1.0 = default (full).

entries.ui_path: VRayLuminaire ▸ Options ▸ Affect atmosph.
entries.notes: Atmospheric contribution amount of the luminaire. 1.0 = default (full).

entries.ui_path: VRayLuminaire ▸ Options ▸ Cast shadows
entries.notes: Whether the luminaire casts shadows. on = default.

entries.ui_path: VRayLuminaire ▸ Sampling ▸ Filtering
entries.notes: Enables sampling filtering (paired with a 3.0 amount spinner). on = default. Sampling detail — display-only.

entries.ui_path: VRayLuminaire ▸ Sampling ▸ Shadow bias
entries.notes: Offsets shadows to avoid self-shadowing. Sampling detail — display-only.

entries.ui_path: VRayAmbientLight ▸ Enabled
entries.notes: Master on/off for the ambient light (adds a flat ambient term). on = default.

entries.ui_path: VRayAmbientLight ▸ Mode
entries.notes: Options: Direct + GI | Direct only | GI only — where the ambient term applies. Direct + GI = default.

entries.ui_path: VRayAmbientLight ▸ GI min distance
entries.notes: Minimum distance used for the GI-based ambient term. 0 = default.

entries.ui_path: VRayAmbientLight ▸ Color
entries.notes: Ambient light color. black = default (no ambient lift). Set a low grey to lift crushed shadows uniformly. Emit as a color instruction.

entries.ui_path: VRayAmbientLight ▸ Intensity
entries.notes: Ambient intensity multiplier (only meaningful once Color is above black). 1.0 = default.

entries.ui_path: VRayAmbientLight ▸ Light map
entries.notes: Enables a light-map contribution (paired with a 100.0 amount spinner). on = default. Folded amount default 100.0.

entries.ui_path: VRayAmbientLight ▸ Compensate exposure
entries.notes: Compensates the ambient term for camera exposure. off = default.

entries.ui_path: Render Setup ▸ V-Ray tab ▸ Environment rollout ▸ GI Environment (Skylight) ▸ On
entries.notes: Options: on | off. Enables the GI environment (skylight) override; while off, the 3ds Max Environment dialog drives GI (docs).

entries.ui_path: Render Setup ▸ V-Ray tab ▸ Environment rollout ▸ GI Environment (Skylight) ▸ Multiplier
entries.notes: Practical range; UI spinner accepts far higher. Multiplies the override Color only — it does NOT affect an assigned environment texture (docs: use an Output map for texture brightness).

entries.ui_path: VRayLight (Dome) ▸ Modify panel ▸ General rollout ▸ Map (texture slot)
entries.notes: Load the HDRI via a VRayBitmap map in this slot; a texture overrides the light's Color/Temperature (docs). Value = HDRI file or mood description, not a number.

entries.ui_path: VRayLight (Dome) ▸ Modify panel ▸ General rollout ▸ Multiplier
entries.notes: Practical range; UI accepts higher. With Units = Default (image) the multiplier scales the HDRI brightness directly. Factory creation value not stated in current Chaos docs (1.0 assumed).

entries.ui_path: Dome HDRI: VRayBitmap ▸ Mapping ▸ Horiz. rotation
entries.notes: Rotates the environment map left/right; ignored when Mapping type = 3ds Max standard (docs). Alternative: rotate the Dome light icon with Dome Light rollout ▸ Lock texture to icon enabled.

entries.ui_path: VRayLight (Dome) ▸ Modify panel ▸ General rollout ▸ Temperature (Mode = Temperature)
entries.notes: Tints an UNtextured dome; any Map in the texture slot overrides color (docs). Kelvin field active only when Mode = Temperature. Factory value not stated in current Chaos docs (6500 assumed).

entries.ui_path: VRayLight (Dome) ▸ Modify panel ▸ Options rollout ▸ Invisible
entries.notes: Options: on | off. Hides the dome from camera/refraction rays only; it still lights the scene and is still seen by GI rays (docs).

entries.ui_path: VRayLight (Plane) ▸ Modify panel ▸ General rollout ▸ Multiplier
entries.notes: Fill-workflow lever for the plane light's Multiplier (same control as light.multiplier). With Units = Default (image) the intensity also depends on the light's SIZE (docs). Default 30.0 confirmed from the UI capture. Practical range; UI accepts higher.

entries.ui_path: VRayLight (Plane) ▸ Modify panel ▸ General rollout ▸ Temperature (Mode = Temperature)
entries.notes: Fill-workflow lever for the plane light's Temperature (same control as light.temperature). Kelvin field active only when Mode = Temperature (docs). 6500 K = neutral daylight.

entries.ui_path: VRayLight (Sphere) ▸ Modify panel ▸ General rollout ▸ Multiplier
entries.notes: Sphere size affects intensity with Default (image) / Luminance / Radiance units (docs). Practical range; UI accepts higher. Factory creation value not stated in current Chaos docs (30 assumed).

entries.ui_path: Create menu ▸ Lights ▸ V-Ray ▸ V-Ray Plane/Sphere Light ▸ click and drag in a viewport
entries.notes: Guidance entry: emit fill placement (position/aim relative to the key light) plus a key:fill intensity ratio — e.g. 4:1 reads moody, 2:1 reads soft. Rendered as an instruction row, not a spinner.

entries.ui_path: VRayPhysicalCamera ▸ Modify panel ▸ Aperture ▸ Film speed (ISO)
entries.notes: Higher = brighter (docs: a V-Ray Sun day scene looks best around 100 ISO). Affects brightness when Exposure = Physical Exposure. Practical range. Factory default not stated in current Chaos docs (100 assumed).

entries.ui_path: VRayPhysicalCamera ▸ Modify panel ▸ Aperture ▸ F-Number
entries.notes: Lower = brighter + more DOF (docs). Affects brightness only when Exposure = Physical Exposure. Practical range. Factory default not stated in current Chaos docs (8.0 assumed).

entries.ui_path: VRayPhysicalCamera ▸ Modify panel ▸ Aperture ▸ Shutter speed (s^-1)
entries.notes: Inverse seconds: 30 means 1/30 s (docs); LOWER value = brighter image. Practical range. Factory default not stated in current Chaos docs (200 assumed).

entries.ui_path: VRayPhysicalCamera ▸ Modify panel ▸ Color & Exposure ▸ Temperature (K) (White balance = Temperature)
entries.notes: Kelvin field applies only when the White balance dropdown = Temperature (docs); presets such as Daylight also exist. Factory value not stated in current Chaos docs (6500 assumed).

entries.ui_path: VRayPhysicalCamera ▸ Modify panel ▸ Color & Exposure ▸ Exposure value
entries.notes: derived: with Exposure = Physical Exposure this field is a greyed-out readout computed from ISO/F-Number/Shutter (docs); it is editable only when Exposure = Exposure Value (EV). Default shown is the approximate factory readout.

entries.ui_path: Render Setup ▸ V-Ray tab ▸ Color mapping rollout ▸ Type
entries.notes: Options: Linear multiply | Exponential | HSV exponential | Intensity exponential | Gamma correction (deprecated) | Intensity gamma (deprecated) | Reinhard. Factory default is Reinhard with Burn value 1.0 = linear result (docs).

entries.ui_path: Render Setup ▸ V-Ray tab ▸ Color mapping rollout ▸ Burn value (Type = Reinhard)
entries.notes: Doc-stated range and default: 1.0 = Linear multiply, 0.0 = Exponential, in-between blends the two (docs). Lower it to tame blown highlights at the render level.

entries.ui_path: V-Ray Frame Buffer ▸ Layers panel ▸ Exposure layer ▸ Contrast
entries.notes: 0 = no change; positive pushes colors away from mid grey, negative toward it (docs). Practical range; slider bounds not stated in docs. Display-side: keep identical across attempts. Layer is not in the VFB's default stack — add it via V-Ray Frame Buffer ▸ Layers panel ▸ + (Add layer) if not present (docs).

entries.ui_path: V-Ray Frame Buffer ▸ Layers panel ▸ Exposure layer ▸ Exposure
entries.notes: Doc-stated default 0.0 = original brightness; +1.0 doubles, -1.0 halves (docs). Practical range; slider bounds not stated in docs. Display-side only — keep identical across attempts. Layer is not in the VFB's default stack — add it via V-Ray Frame Buffer ▸ Layers panel ▸ + (Add layer) if not present (docs).

entries.ui_path: V-Ray Frame Buffer ▸ Layers panel ▸ Hue/Saturation layer ▸ Saturation
entries.notes: Lower moves toward greyscale, higher intensifies colors (docs); 0 = no change. Display-side: keep identical across attempts. Layer is not in the VFB's default stack — add it via V-Ray Frame Buffer ▸ Layers panel ▸ + (Add layer) if not present (docs). Range −100..100: the Chaos-Player HSL color-correction docs (same VFB/Player family) state Saturation −100..+∞, so a ±100-scale is the right order of magnitude here — NOT the −1..1 the separate Vantage product uses (that Vantage value was in-product confirmed and is product-specific). Definitive VFB bounds still want a live glance, but this is NOT the 100x twin of the Vantage bug.

sheet.group: V-Ray Frame Buffer · White Balance layer

entries.ui_path: V-Ray Frame Buffer ▸ Layers panel ▸ White Balance layer ▸ Temperature
entries.group: V-Ray Frame Buffer · White Balance layer
entries.notes: Lower = bluer, higher = more amber (docs). 6500 K = layer-neutral (no correction; derived, not doc-stated). Pairs with the Magenta - Green tint slider in the same layer. Practical range. Layer is not in the VFB's default stack — add it via V-Ray Frame Buffer ▸ Layers panel ▸ + (Add layer) if not present (docs).

entries.ui_path: Render Setup ▸ GI tab ▸ Global illumination rollout ▸ Primary engine
entries.notes: Options: Irradiance map (deprecated, slated for removal) | Brute force | Light cache. Factory default: Brute force (docs, Universal V-Ray Settings). Notes-only: engine choice changes noise/speed character, not the lighting targets.

entries.ui_path: Render Setup ▸ GI tab ▸ Global illumination rollout ▸ Secondary engine
entries.notes: Options: None | Brute force | Light cache. Factory default: Light cache (docs). Brute force defaults to 3 bounces, Light cache works with ~100 (docs); None removes indirect color bleeding.

entries.ui_path: Rendering menu ▸ Environment ▸ Add ▸ VRayEnvironmentFog
entries.notes: Options: on | off. on = the VRayEnvironmentFog atmospheric effect is added via the docs' Add path; off = effect absent (neutral — no fog). Without gizmos it fills the scene below Fog height (docs). Docs recommend turning on Optimized atmospherics evaluation (Render Setup ▸ System rollout) with it.

entries.ui_path: VRayEnvironmentFog ▸ General parameters ▸ Fog color
entries.notes: Color swatch (texture-mappable): how the fog reacts to light — it does NOT change the volume transparency (docs). white = untinted scattering (derived neutral; factory value not printed). Emit as an instruction, e.g. 'pale warm grey for dusty evening air'.

entries.ui_path: VRayEnvironmentFog ▸ General parameters ▸ Fog distance
entries.notes: THE density control: larger = more transparent fog, smaller = denser (docs). Value in 3ds Max scene units (no fixed unit stated in docs); practical range. Factory creation value not printed in current Chaos docs (50 assumed — the docs' Fog height example pairs distance 50 with height 10).

entries.ui_path: VRayEnvironmentFog ▸ General parameters ▸ Fog height
entries.notes: Z-level the fog starts at, continuing downward indefinitely; IGNORED when gizmos are listed in the Nodes section (docs). Raising it darkens the scene (more fog blocks the sun) — compensate by raising Fog distance (docs). Factory value not printed (10 assumed, doc example).

entries.ui_path: VRayEnvironmentFog ▸ General parameters ▸ Fog phase function
entries.notes: Doc-stated default 0.0 = uniform scattering; positive = forward scatter (glow around backlights), negative = backward (docs). Docs warn values very close to +/-1.0 produce very directional scattering — practical range stops at 0.9.

entries.ui_path: VRayEnvironmentFog ▸ General parameters ▸ Scatter GI
entries.notes: Options: on | off. When on, the fog scatters global illumination using the current GI engine — can be quite slow; docs suggest a simple Fog emission term as the substitute. Factory state not printed in current Chaos docs (off assumed). Folded sub-params (docs): Scatter bounces (active only while on; the dense-smoke example uses 100) and the Fog emission color swatch (fog self-illumination, the cheap GI substitute).

entries.ui_path: Rendering menu ▸ Environment ▸ Add ▸ VRayAerialPerspective
entries.notes: Options: on | off. Distance-haze approximation that works together with VRaySun + VRaySky; renders faster than VRayEnvironmentFog but produces no volumetric shadows (docs). off = effect absent (neutral). The sun's Affect atmospherics option has NO effect on it (docs, VRaySun page). Folded sub-toggle: Affect environment rays (doc default OFF — the VRaySky already accounts for scattered sunlight; enable only for artistic low-visibility looks, docs).

entries.ui_path: VRayAerialPerspective ▸ Parameters ▸ Visibility range (in meters)
entries.notes: Distance at which the haze has absorbed 90% of the light from objects behind it; lower = denser (docs). ALWAYS meters — converted internally from the current 3ds Max units (docs). Factory default not printed (10000 assumed; the docs' small demo scene uses 30-540 m).

entries.ui_path: VRayAerialPerspective ▸ Parameters ▸ Atmosphere height (in meters)
entries.notes: Height of the atmosphere layer in meters, converted internally from the scene units; lower values exaggerate the effect artistically and interact with scene scale (docs). Factory default not printed (10000 assumed). Practical range.

entries.ui_path: VRayAerialPerspective ▸ Parameters ▸ Inscattered light intensity
entries.notes: Doc-stated default 1.0 = physically accurate amount of sunlight scattered into the haze; lower/higher only for artistic purposes (docs). Practical range; spinner bounds not stated in docs.

entries.ui_path: VRayAerialPerspective ▸ Parameters ▸ Filter color
entries.notes: Color swatch tinting the inscattered light (docs; their example shifts the hue of a red filter). white = untinted (derived neutral). Emit as an instruction, e.g. 'pale warm filter for golden-hour haze'.

entries.ui_path: VRayAerialPerspective ▸ Parameters ▸ Affect background
entries.notes: Options: on | off. Doc-stated default ON — the haze also covers camera rays that hit a background other than VRaySky; disabling gives cut-out looks (docs).

vray7max.promptFragment:
TARGET: V-Ray 7 for 3ds Max. Allowed parameter ids — choose ONLY from these; numeric values must stay inside the stated ranges:
sun.enabled — VRaySun ▸ Sun parameters ▸ Enabled — kind:checkbox default:"on" — Master on/off for the physical sun. off = no direct sun contribution (neutral off-state).
sun.intensity_mult — VRaySun ▸ Sun parameters ▸ Intensity multiplier — kind:spinner unit:x range:[0,2] default:1 — 1.0 = physical solar brightness; docs recommend keeping it and exposing via camera or color mapping. Values like 0.01-0.05 only when NO exposure control is used. UI accepts higher than 2 (practical range).
sun.size_mult — VRaySun ▸ Sun parameters ▸ Size multiplier — kind:spinner unit:x range:[0.2,40] default:1 — Visible sun-disc size AND shadow-edge softness; overall illumination strength stays the same (docs). 1.0 = real sun; docs examples use 4-40 for visibly soft shadows. Practical range; UI accepts higher.
sun.filter_color — VRaySun ▸ Sun parameters ▸ Filter color — kind:color default:"white" — Tints the sun color (active as the tint in Filter mode, as the whole color in override mode). white = physical/untinted. Emit as a color instruction, e.g. 'warm amber for late-afternoon sun'.
sun.color_mode — VRaySun ▸ Sun parameters ▸ Color mode — kind:dropdown default:"Filter" — Options: Filter | Direct | Override. Filter tints the physical color, Direct/Override replace it. V-Ray 7's sun has NO Kelvin field — warmth comes from elevation + Turbidity + Ozone, or Direct/Override with a warm Filter color (docs).
sun.kelvin — VRaySun ▸ Sun parameters ▸ Color mode + Filter color — kind:placement unit:K range:[1000,20000] default:5777 — V-Ray 7's VRaySun has NO Kelvin spinner — Color mode options are filter | direct | override (docs) and sun color is physical (elevation + Turbidity + Ozone). To hit a target kelvin: lower the elevation / raise Turbidity for warmth, or set Color mode = direct with a warm Filter color; numeric kelvin white balance lives on the camera (cam.wb_kelvin). 5777 K = physical solar temperature, informational.
sun.placement_azimuth — VRaySun ▸ move/rotate the sun head in the viewport, or Create panel ▸ Systems ▸ Daylight ▸ Sunlight = VRaySun ▸ Position (Date/Time/Location or Manual) — kind:placement unit:deg range:[0,360] default:135 — V-Ray 7 has no azimuth spinner on VRaySun itself — position is set by moving the sun or via a 3ds Max Daylight system with VRaySun as the sun type (docs). Compass: 0 = North, 90 = East. Emit as a placement instruction; default is informational.
sun.placement_elevation — VRaySun ▸ move the sun head height in the viewport, or Create panel ▸ Systems ▸ Daylight ▸ Sunlight = VRaySun ▸ Position (Date/Time/Location or Manual) — kind:placement unit:deg range:[-12,90] default:35 — Elevation above horizon; sun and sky color follow the position physically — a lower sun is warmer with longer, softer-lit shadows (docs). Negative elevations reach twilight/dusk: the sun drops below the horizon and the PRG Clear Sky model keeps producing sky illumination down to about -12 deg (civil-to-nautical dusk), so a dusk reference is matched by placing the sun a few degrees under the horizon rather than clamping at 0. Emit as a placement instruction; default is informational.
sun.sky_model — VRaySun ▸ Sky parameters ▸ Sky model — kind:dropdown default:"PRG Clear Sky" — Options: Preetham et al. | CIE Clear | CIE Overcast | Hosek et al. | PRG Clear Sky (old) | PRG Clear Sky. For a fully overcast grey sky choose CIE Overcast. PRG Clear Sky is the modern physical model (twilight to -12 deg).
sun.ground_albedo — VRaySun ▸ Sky parameters ▸ Ground Albedo — kind:color default:"gray" — Reflectivity/color of the virtual ground bounced back into the sky. gray = neutral default. A warm/green albedo subtly tints skylight fill. Emit as a color instruction when the reference ground clearly bounces color into the scene.
sun.indirect_horiz_illum — VRaySun ▸ Sky parameters ▸ Indirect horiz illum — kind:spinner unit:lx range:[0,200000] default:25000 — Intensity (in lux) of illumination on horizontal surfaces coming from the sky; scales overall skylight brightness. 25000 = default clear-day value. Practical range.
sun.blend_angle — VRaySun ▸ Sky parameters ▸ Blend angle — kind:spinner unit:deg range:[0,90] default:0.1 — Angle (deg) over which the horizon blends into the sky, softening the horizon line. 0.1 = default sharp horizon. Raise for a hazier horizon transition.
sun.horizon_offset — VRaySun ▸ Sky parameters ▸ Horizon offset — kind:spinner unit:deg range:[-90,90] default:0 — Lowers/raises the horizon line manually (deg). 0 = physical horizon. Use to hide a low horizon or tuck the sky behind geometry.
sun.turbidity — VRaySun ▸ Sky parameters ▸ Turbidity — kind:spinner range:[2,20] default:2.5 — Air dust: 2 = clear blue sky/sun, 8+ = yellow-orange haze (docs examples 2-8). Affects sun AND sky color. Practical range; UI accepts higher. Default 2.5 confirmed from the UI capture (2026-07-03; pack previously assumed 3.0).
sun.ozone — VRaySun ▸ Sky parameters ▸ Ozone — kind:spinner range:[0,1] default:0.35 — Ozone in the air (0-1): higher shifts the sun's light bluer, lower makes it more yellow/red. 0.35 = default. Works alongside Turbidity for sun/sky warmth.
sun.altitude — VRaySun ▸ Sky parameters ▸ Altitude — kind:spinner unit:m range:[0,100000] default:0 — Observer altitude above sea level (m) for the PRG Clear Sky model; higher altitude thins the atmosphere. 0 = sea level. Subtle sky-color effect.
sun.night_blueness — VRaySun ▸ Sky parameters ▸ Night blueness — kind:spinner range:[0,1] default:0 — How blue the sky appears at night / very low sun (0-1). 0 = default. Raise for a bluer twilight/night sky.
clouds.on — VRaySun ▸ Clouds ▸ Clouds on — kind:checkbox default:"off" — Master on/off for V-Ray 7's procedural clouds (a section of the SUN — the VRaySky texture has no cloud params and follows the sun). off = clear sky (neutral). For fully overcast, prefer Sky model = CIE Overcast.
clouds.ground_shadows — VRaySun ▸ Clouds ▸ Ground shadows — kind:checkbox default:"off" — off = one global lit/shadowed state decided at the camera position (fast, small scenes); on = precise per-point cloud shadows, slower but defined — for larger scenes (docs). NOTE: Vantage's same-named toggle means cloud shadows on/off instead.
clouds.density — VRaySun ▸ Clouds ▸ Density — kind:spinner range:[0,1] default:0.5 — Density of the cumulus/stratus clouds: 1 fills up the sky (docs; examples 0/0.4/0.8). Default 0.5 confirmed from the UI capture.
clouds.density_mult — VRaySun ▸ Clouds ▸ Density multiplier — kind:spinner unit:x range:[0,5] default:1 — Multiplier on Density; larger values darken the sky at the horizon, 0 removes all clouds regardless of Density (docs). 1.0 = neutral multiplier. Practical range.
clouds.variety — VRaySun ▸ Clouds ▸ Variety — kind:spinner range:[0,1] default:0.3 — Variety of the cumulus/stratus cloud pattern (docs; examples 0/0.5/1). Default 0.3 confirmed from the UI capture.
clouds.cirrus_amount — VRaySun ▸ Clouds ▸ Cirrus amount — kind:spinner range:[0,1] default:0.2 — Doc-stated scale: maximum 1 fills the sky with cirrus (high, wispy), 0 = cirrus gone. Default 0.2 confirmed from the UI capture.
clouds.offset_x — VRaySun ▸ Clouds ▸ Offset X (m) — kind:spinner unit:m range:[-100000,100000] default:0 — Slides the whole cloud system along X (m). 0 = default. Use to move a cloud mass out of / into frame.
clouds.offset_y — VRaySun ▸ Clouds ▸ Offset Y (m) — kind:spinner unit:m range:[-100000,100000] default:0 — Slides the whole cloud system along Y (m). 0 = default. Pairs with Offset X to reposition clouds.
clouds.height — VRaySun ▸ Clouds ▸ Height (m) — kind:spinner unit:m range:[100,10000] default:1000 — Clouds position in height, meters (docs; examples 500/1000/1500). Default 1000 confirmed from the UI capture.
clouds.thickness — VRaySun ▸ Clouds ▸ Thickness (m) — kind:spinner unit:m range:[10,5000] default:300 — Lower = thin, sheer cumulus/stratus; higher = full and heavy (docs; examples 200/500/800). Default 300 confirmed from the UI capture.
clouds.phase_x — VRaySun ▸ Clouds ▸ Phase X (%) — kind:spinner unit:% range:[0,200] default:0 — Fine-tweaks the cumulus/stratus pattern along X and LOOPS at 0/100/200 (%). 0 = default. Small pattern nudge that keeps overall coverage.
clouds.phase_y — VRaySun ▸ Clouds ▸ Phase Y (%) — kind:spinner unit:% range:[0,200] default:0 — Fine-tweaks the cumulus/stratus pattern along Y and LOOPS at 0/100/200 (%). 0 = default. Pairs with Phase X.
clouds.enable_contrails — VRaySun ▸ Clouds ▸ Enable contrails — kind:checkbox default:"off" — Adds aircraft contrails across the sky. off = none (neutral). Enable only when the reference clearly shows contrails; the sub-params below stay inactive until this is on.
sun.invisible — VRaySun ▸ Options ▸ Invisible — kind:checkbox default:"off" — Hides the sun disc from camera rays only; it still lights the scene. off = sun disc visible (neutral). Turn on to keep a bright sun out of frame while retaining its light.
sun.affect_diffuse — VRaySun ▸ Options ▸ Affect diffuse — kind:checkbox default:"on" — Whether the sun contributes to diffuse shading (paired with a 1.0 amount spinner). on = default. Rarely turned off; folded amount default 1.0.
sun.affect_specular — VRaySun ▸ Options ▸ Affect specular — kind:checkbox default:"on" — Whether the sun contributes specular highlights (paired with a 1.0 amount spinner). on = default. Folded amount default 1.0.
sun.affect_atmos — VRaySun ▸ Options ▸ Affect atmos. — kind:checkbox default:"on" — Whether the sun lights atmospheric effects/fog (paired with a 1.0 amount spinner). on = default. Has NO effect on VRayAerialPerspective (docs). Folded amount default 1.0.
sun.cast_atmos_shadows — VRaySun ▸ Options ▸ Cast atmospheric shadows — kind:checkbox default:"on" — Whether the sun casts shadows through atmospheric volumes (light shafts through fog). on = default.
light.on — VRayLight ▸ General ▸ On — kind:checkbox default:"on" — Master on/off for the area (plane) light. on = default. off removes the light.
light.type — VRayLight ▸ General ▸ Type — kind:dropdown default:"Plane" — Options: Plane | Disc | Sphere | Dome | Mesh. Plane = default rectangular area light. Type changes which rollouts apply.
light.length — VRayLight ▸ General ▸ Length — kind:spinner unit:units range:[0,100000] default:20 — Plane light length (scene units). With Units = Default (image) the SIZE also scales the effective intensity. 20 = default. Larger = softer light + shadows.
light.width — VRayLight ▸ General ▸ Width — kind:spinner unit:units range:[0,100000] default:20 — Plane light width (scene units). With Units = Default (image) the SIZE also scales the effective intensity. 20 = default. Pairs with Length for the softbox size.
light.units — VRayLight ▸ General ▸ Units — kind:dropdown default:"Default (image)" — Options: Default (image) | Luminous power (lm) | Luminance (lm/m²/sr) | Radiant power (W) | Radiance (W/m²/sr). Default (image) makes Multiplier size-dependent; photometric units make it size-independent.
light.multiplier — VRayLight ▸ General ▸ Multiplier — kind:spinner unit:x range:[0,500] default:30 — Brightness of the plane/area light; with Units = Default (image) it also depends on the light's SIZE. Default 30.0 confirmed from the UI capture. Practical range; UI accepts higher. (The fill-workflow lever fill.plane_intensity targets this same control.)
light.mode — VRayLight ▸ General ▸ Mode — kind:dropdown default:"Color" — Options: Color | Temperature. Color uses the color swatch; Temperature enables the Kelvin field below. Color = default.
light.color — VRayLight ▸ General ▸ Color — kind:color default:"white" — Light color (active when Mode = Color). white = neutral. Emit as a color instruction to warm/cool a fill.
light.temperature — VRayLight ▸ General ▸ Temperature (Mode = Temperature) — kind:spinner unit:K range:[1000,20000] default:6500 — Kelvin color of the light; active only when Mode = Temperature. 6500 K = neutral daylight. Lower = warmer fill.
light.map — VRayLight ▸ General ▸ Map — kind:slot default:"none" — Texture slot (with an on/off checkbox) projected by the light; a map overrides Color/Temperature. none = no texture. Value = texture file or mood description, not a number.
light.directional — VRayLight ▸ Plane/disc light ▸ Directional — kind:spinner range:[0,1] default:0 — Focuses the plane light into a more directional beam (0 = full hemisphere spread, 1 = tight). 0 = default soft area light.
light.directional_strength — VRayLight ▸ Plane/disc light ▸ Directional strength — kind:spinner range:[0,1] default:0.9 — Strength of the directional focusing above. 0.9 = default. Interacts with Directional to shape falloff.
light.cast_shadows — VRayLight ▸ Options ▸ Cast shadows — kind:checkbox default:"on" — Whether the light casts shadows. on = default. Turn off for a pure fill that adds no shadowing.
light.double_sided — VRayLight ▸ Options ▸ Double-sided — kind:checkbox default:"off" — Emits from both faces of the plane instead of one. off = default (one-sided). Turn on to light from both sides.
light.invisible — VRayLight ▸ Options ▸ Invisible — kind:checkbox default:"off" — Hides the light shape from camera rays; it still lights the scene. off = default (shape visible). Turn on to keep a fill out of frame.
light.affect_diffuse — VRayLight ▸ Options ▸ Affect diffuse — kind:checkbox default:"on" — Whether the light contributes to diffuse shading (paired with a 1.0 amount spinner). on = default. Folded amount default 1.0.
light.affect_specular — VRayLight ▸ Options ▸ Affect specular — kind:checkbox default:"on" — Whether the light contributes specular highlights (paired with a 1.0 amount spinner). on = default. Turn off to kill a fill's highlights. Folded amount default 1.0.
light.affect_reflections — VRayLight ▸ Options ▸ Affect reflections — kind:checkbox default:"on" — Whether the light shows up in reflections. on = default. Turn off so a fill does not appear as a reflected softbox.
light.affect_atmos — VRayLight ▸ Options ▸ Affect atmos. — kind:checkbox default:"on" — Whether the light lights atmospheric effects/fog (paired with a 1.0 amount spinner). on = default. Folded amount default 1.0.
ies.enabled — VRayIES ▸ General ▸ Enabled — kind:checkbox default:"on" — Master on/off for the IES photometric light. on = default. off removes it.
ies.targeted — VRayIES ▸ General ▸ Targeted — kind:checkbox default:"on" — Whether the IES light uses a target node to aim. on = default. Placement/aim behavior.
ies.file — VRayIES ▸ General ▸ IES file — kind:slot default:"none" — The .ies photometric profile file. none = unset. Value = IES file or fixture description; the profile shapes the beam.
ies.intensity_value — VRayIES ▸ Intensity and color ▸ Intensity value — kind:spinner unit:lm range:[0,1000000] default:1700 — Luminous intensity (units per Intensity type). 1700 = default. Raise/lower to match fixture brightness.
ies.intensity_type — VRayIES ▸ Intensity and color ▸ Intensity type — kind:dropdown default:"power (lm)" — Options: power (lm) | candelas (cd) | ... — the unit that Intensity value is expressed in. power (lm) = default.
ies.override_intensity — VRayIES ▸ Intensity and color ▸ Override intensity — kind:dropdown default:"rescale" — Options: rescale | replace | none — how the Intensity value interacts with the value baked into the IES file. rescale = default.
ies.color_mode — VRayIES ▸ Intensity and color ▸ Color mode — kind:dropdown default:"Color" — Options: Color | Temperature. Color uses the swatch; Temperature enables the Kelvin field. Color = default.
ies.color — VRayIES ▸ Intensity and color ▸ Color — kind:color default:"magenta" — IES light color (active when Color mode = Color). Capture shows magenta as the current value. Emit as a color instruction; set to a neutral/warm fixture tone to match.
ies.color_temp — VRayIES ▸ Intensity and color ▸ Color temperature — kind:spinner unit:K range:[1000,20000] default:6500 — Kelvin color; active only when Color mode = Temperature. 6500 K = neutral daylight.
ies.cast_shadows — VRayIES ▸ Options ▸ Cast shadows — kind:checkbox default:"on" — Whether the IES light casts shadows. on = default.
ies.affect_diffuse — VRayIES ▸ Options ▸ Affect diffuse — kind:checkbox default:"on" — Whether the IES light contributes diffuse (paired 1.0 amount). on = default.
ies.affect_specular — VRayIES ▸ Options ▸ Affect specular — kind:checkbox default:"on" — Whether the IES light contributes specular (paired 1.0 amount). on = default.
ies.affect_atmos — VRayIES ▸ Options ▸ Affect atmos. — kind:checkbox default:"on" — Whether the IES light lights atmosphere/fog (paired 1.0 amount). on = default.
ies.use_light_shape — VRayIES ▸ Options ▸ Use light shape — kind:dropdown default:"For shadow" — Options: For shadow | Always | Never — whether the IES-defined shape is used for shadowing/illumination. For shadow = default.
lum.enabled — VRayLuminaire ▸ General ▸ Enabled — kind:checkbox default:"on" — Master on/off for the luminaire (packaged fixture). on = default.
lum.file — VRayLuminaire ▸ General ▸ Luminaire file — kind:slot default:"none" — The luminaire definition file. none = unset. Value = file or fixture description.
lum.scale — VRayLuminaire ▸ General ▸ Scale — kind:spinner unit:x range:[0,1000] default:1 — Geometric scale of the luminaire. 1.0 = default. Larger physical fixture.
lum.intensity — VRayLuminaire ▸ Intensity and color ▸ Intensity — kind:spinner unit:x range:[0,1000] default:1 — Brightness multiplier of the luminaire. 1.0 = default. Raise/lower to match fixture output.
lum.color_mode — VRayLuminaire ▸ Intensity and color ▸ Color mode — kind:dropdown default:"Color" — Options: Color | Temperature. Color = default; Temperature enables the Kelvin field.
lum.color — VRayLuminaire ▸ Intensity and color ▸ Color — kind:color default:"white" — Luminaire color (active when Color mode = Color). white = neutral. Emit as a color instruction.
lum.color_temp — VRayLuminaire ▸ Intensity and color ▸ Color temperature — kind:spinner unit:K range:[1000,20000] default:6500 — Kelvin color; active only when Color mode = Temperature. 6500 K = neutral daylight (inactive at default).
lum.affect_diffuse — VRayLuminaire ▸ Options ▸ Affect diffuse — kind:spinner range:[0,1] default:1 — Diffuse contribution amount of the luminaire. 1.0 = default (full).
lum.affect_specular — VRayLuminaire ▸ Options ▸ Affect specular — kind:spinner range:[0,1] default:1 — Specular contribution amount of the luminaire. 1.0 = default (full).
lum.affect_atmos — VRayLuminaire ▸ Options ▸ Affect atmosph. — kind:spinner range:[0,1] default:1 — Atmospheric contribution amount of the luminaire. 1.0 = default (full).
lum.cast_shadows — VRayLuminaire ▸ Options ▸ Cast shadows — kind:checkbox default:"on" — Whether the luminaire casts shadows. on = default.
amb.enabled — VRayAmbientLight ▸ Enabled — kind:checkbox default:"on" — Master on/off for the ambient light (adds a flat ambient term). on = default.
amb.mode — VRayAmbientLight ▸ Mode — kind:dropdown default:"Direct + GI" — Options: Direct + GI | Direct only | GI only — where the ambient term applies. Direct + GI = default.
amb.gi_min_distance — VRayAmbientLight ▸ GI min distance — kind:spinner unit:units range:[0,100000] default:0 — Minimum distance used for the GI-based ambient term. 0 = default.
amb.color — VRayAmbientLight ▸ Color — kind:color default:"black" — Ambient light color. black = default (no ambient lift). Set a low grey to lift crushed shadows uniformly. Emit as a color instruction.
amb.intensity — VRayAmbientLight ▸ Intensity — kind:spinner unit:x range:[0,100] default:1 — Ambient intensity multiplier (only meaningful once Color is above black). 1.0 = default.
amb.light_map — VRayAmbientLight ▸ Light map — kind:checkbox default:"on" — Enables a light-map contribution (paired with a 100.0 amount spinner). on = default. Folded amount default 100.0.
amb.compensate_exposure — VRayAmbientLight ▸ Compensate exposure — kind:checkbox default:"off" — Compensates the ambient term for camera exposure. off = default.
env.gi_skylight_on — Render Setup ▸ V-Ray tab ▸ Environment rollout ▸ GI Environment (Skylight) ▸ On — kind:dropdown default:"off" — Options: on | off. Enables the GI environment (skylight) override; while off, the 3ds Max Environment dialog drives GI (docs).
env.gi_skylight_mult — Render Setup ▸ V-Ray tab ▸ Environment rollout ▸ GI Environment (Skylight) ▸ Multiplier — kind:spinner unit:x range:[0,20] default:1 — Practical range; UI spinner accepts far higher. Multiplies the override Color only — it does NOT affect an assigned environment texture (docs: use an Output map for texture brightness).
dome.texture_slot — VRayLight (Dome) ▸ Modify panel ▸ General rollout ▸ Map (texture slot) — kind:slot default:"none" — Load the HDRI via a VRayBitmap map in this slot; a texture overrides the light's Color/Temperature (docs). Value = HDRI file or mood description, not a number.
dome.intensity — VRayLight (Dome) ▸ Modify panel ▸ General rollout ▸ Multiplier — kind:spinner unit:x range:[0,100] default:1 — Practical range; UI accepts higher. With Units = Default (image) the multiplier scales the HDRI brightness directly. Factory creation value not stated in current Chaos docs (1.0 assumed).
dome.rotation_h — Dome HDRI: VRayBitmap ▸ Mapping ▸ Horiz. rotation — kind:spinner unit:deg range:[0,360] default:0 — Rotates the environment map left/right; ignored when Mapping type = 3ds Max standard (docs). Alternative: rotate the Dome light icon with Dome Light rollout ▸ Lock texture to icon enabled.
dome.invisible — VRayLight (Dome) ▸ Modify panel ▸ Options rollout ▸ Invisible — kind:dropdown default:"off" — Options: on | off. Hides the dome from camera/refraction rays only; it still lights the scene and is still seen by GI rays (docs).
dome.temperature — VRayLight (Dome) ▸ Modify panel ▸ General rollout ▸ Temperature (Mode = Temperature) — kind:spinner unit:K range:[1000,20000] default:6500 — Tints an UNtextured dome; any Map in the texture slot overrides color (docs). Kelvin field active only when Mode = Temperature. Factory value not stated in current Chaos docs (6500 assumed).
fill.plane_intensity — VRayLight (Plane) ▸ Modify panel ▸ General rollout ▸ Multiplier — kind:spinner unit:x range:[0,500] default:30 — Fill-workflow lever for the plane light's Multiplier (same control as light.multiplier). With Units = Default (image) the intensity also depends on the light's SIZE (docs). Default 30.0 confirmed from the UI capture. Practical range; UI accepts higher.
fill.plane_kelvin — VRayLight (Plane) ▸ Modify panel ▸ General rollout ▸ Temperature (Mode = Temperature) — kind:spinner unit:K range:[1000,20000] default:6500 — Fill-workflow lever for the plane light's Temperature (same control as light.temperature). Kelvin field active only when Mode = Temperature (docs). 6500 K = neutral daylight.
fill.sphere_intensity — VRayLight (Sphere) ▸ Modify panel ▸ General rollout ▸ Multiplier — kind:spinner unit:x range:[0,500] default:30 — Sphere size affects intensity with Default (image) / Luminance / Radiance units (docs). Practical range; UI accepts higher. Factory creation value not stated in current Chaos docs (30 assumed).
fill.key_fill_guidance — Create menu ▸ Lights ▸ V-Ray ▸ V-Ray Plane/Sphere Light ▸ click and drag in a viewport — kind:placement unit::1 range:[1,10] default:4 — Guidance entry: emit fill placement (position/aim relative to the key light) plus a key:fill intensity ratio — e.g. 4:1 reads moody, 2:1 reads soft. Rendered as an instruction row, not a spinner.
cam.iso — VRayPhysicalCamera ▸ Modify panel ▸ Aperture ▸ Film speed (ISO) — kind:spinner unit:ISO range:[25,6400] default:100 — Higher = brighter (docs: a V-Ray Sun day scene looks best around 100 ISO). Affects brightness when Exposure = Physical Exposure. Practical range. Factory default not stated in current Chaos docs (100 assumed).
cam.fnumber — VRayPhysicalCamera ▸ Modify panel ▸ Aperture ▸ F-Number — kind:spinner unit:f/ range:[0.7,64] default:8 — Lower = brighter + more DOF (docs). Affects brightness only when Exposure = Physical Exposure. Practical range. Factory default not stated in current Chaos docs (8.0 assumed).
cam.shutter — VRayPhysicalCamera ▸ Modify panel ▸ Aperture ▸ Shutter speed (s^-1) — kind:spinner unit:s^-1 range:[1,2000] default:200 — Inverse seconds: 30 means 1/30 s (docs); LOWER value = brighter image. Practical range. Factory default not stated in current Chaos docs (200 assumed).
cam.wb_kelvin — VRayPhysicalCamera ▸ Modify panel ▸ Color & Exposure ▸ Temperature (K) (White balance = Temperature) — kind:spinner unit:K range:[1000,20000] default:6500 — Kelvin field applies only when the White balance dropdown = Temperature (docs); presets such as Daylight also exist. Factory value not stated in current Chaos docs (6500 assumed).
cam.ev_readout — VRayPhysicalCamera ▸ Modify panel ▸ Color & Exposure ▸ Exposure value — kind:spinner unit:EV range:[-6,26] default:14 — derived: with Exposure = Physical Exposure this field is a greyed-out readout computed from ISO/F-Number/Shutter (docs); it is editable only when Exposure = Exposure Value (EV). Default shown is the approximate factory readout.
cm.type — Render Setup ▸ V-Ray tab ▸ Color mapping rollout ▸ Type — kind:dropdown default:"Reinhard" — Options: Linear multiply | Exponential | HSV exponential | Intensity exponential | Gamma correction (deprecated) | Intensity gamma (deprecated) | Reinhard. Factory default is Reinhard with Burn value 1.0 = linear result (docs).
cm.highlight_burn — Render Setup ▸ V-Ray tab ▸ Color mapping rollout ▸ Burn value (Type = Reinhard) — kind:spinner range:[0,1] default:1 — Doc-stated range and default: 1.0 = Linear multiply, 0.0 = Exponential, in-between blends the two (docs). Lower it to tame blown highlights at the render level.
cm.contrast — V-Ray Frame Buffer ▸ Layers panel ▸ Exposure layer ▸ Contrast — kind:spinner range:[-1,1] default:0 — 0 = no change; positive pushes colors away from mid grey, negative toward it (docs). Practical range; slider bounds not stated in docs. Display-side: keep identical across attempts. Layer is not in the VFB's default stack — add it via V-Ray Frame Buffer ▸ Layers panel ▸ + (Add layer) if not present (docs).
cm.saturation — V-Ray Frame Buffer ▸ Layers panel ▸ Hue/Saturation layer ▸ Saturation — kind:spinner range:[-100,100] default:0 — Lower moves toward greyscale, higher intensifies colors (docs); 0 = no change. Display-side: keep identical across attempts. Layer is not in the VFB's default stack — add it via V-Ray Frame Buffer ▸ Layers panel ▸ + (Add layer) if not present (docs). Range −100..100: the Chaos-Player HSL color-correction docs (same VFB/Player family) state Saturation −100..+∞, so a ±100-scale is the right order of magnitude here — NOT the −1..1 the separate Vantage product uses (that Vantage value was in-product confirmed and is product-specific). Definitive VFB bounds still want a live glance, but this is NOT the 100x twin of the Vantage bug.
vfb.exposure — V-Ray Frame Buffer ▸ Layers panel ▸ Exposure layer ▸ Exposure — kind:spinner unit:stops range:[-5,5] default:0 — Doc-stated default 0.0 = original brightness; +1.0 doubles, -1.0 halves (docs). Practical range; slider bounds not stated in docs. Display-side only — keep identical across attempts. Layer is not in the VFB's default stack — add it via V-Ray Frame Buffer ▸ Layers panel ▸ + (Add layer) if not present (docs).
vfb.wb_kelvin — V-Ray Frame Buffer ▸ Layers panel ▸ White Balance layer ▸ Temperature — kind:spinner unit:K range:[1000,20000] default:6500 — Lower = bluer, higher = more amber (docs). 6500 K = layer-neutral (no correction; derived, not doc-stated). Pairs with the Magenta - Green tint slider in the same layer. Practical range. Layer is not in the VFB's default stack — add it via V-Ray Frame Buffer ▸ Layers panel ▸ + (Add layer) if not present (docs).
fog.enabled — Rendering menu ▸ Environment ▸ Add ▸ VRayEnvironmentFog — kind:dropdown default:"off" — Options: on | off. on = the VRayEnvironmentFog atmospheric effect is added via the docs' Add path; off = effect absent (neutral — no fog). Without gizmos it fills the scene below Fog height (docs). Docs recommend turning on Optimized atmospherics evaluation (Render Setup ▸ System rollout) with it.
fog.color — VRayEnvironmentFog ▸ General parameters ▸ Fog color — kind:color default:"white (untinted)" — Color swatch (texture-mappable): how the fog reacts to light — it does NOT change the volume transparency (docs). white = untinted scattering (derived neutral; factory value not printed). Emit as an instruction, e.g. 'pale warm grey for dusty evening air'.
fog.distance — VRayEnvironmentFog ▸ General parameters ▸ Fog distance — kind:spinner unit:units range:[0.1,10000] default:50 — THE density control: larger = more transparent fog, smaller = denser (docs). Value in 3ds Max scene units (no fixed unit stated in docs); practical range. Factory creation value not printed in current Chaos docs (50 assumed — the docs' Fog height example pairs distance 50 with height 10).
fog.height — VRayEnvironmentFog ▸ General parameters ▸ Fog height — kind:spinner unit:units range:[0,10000] default:10 — Z-level the fog starts at, continuing downward indefinitely; IGNORED when gizmos are listed in the Nodes section (docs). Raising it darkens the scene (more fog blocks the sun) — compensate by raising Fog distance (docs). Factory value not printed (10 assumed, doc example).
fog.phase — VRayEnvironmentFog ▸ General parameters ▸ Fog phase function — kind:spinner range:[-0.9,0.9] default:0 — Doc-stated default 0.0 = uniform scattering; positive = forward scatter (glow around backlights), negative = backward (docs). Docs warn values very close to +/-1.0 produce very directional scattering — practical range stops at 0.9.
fog.scatter_gi — VRayEnvironmentFog ▸ General parameters ▸ Scatter GI — kind:dropdown default:"off" — Options: on | off. When on, the fog scatters global illumination using the current GI engine — can be quite slow; docs suggest a simple Fog emission term as the substitute. Factory state not printed in current Chaos docs (off assumed). Folded sub-params (docs): Scatter bounces (active only while on; the dense-smoke example uses 100) and the Fog emission color swatch (fog self-illumination, the cheap GI substitute).
aerial.enabled — Rendering menu ▸ Environment ▸ Add ▸ VRayAerialPerspective — kind:dropdown default:"off" — Options: on | off. Distance-haze approximation that works together with VRaySun + VRaySky; renders faster than VRayEnvironmentFog but produces no volumetric shadows (docs). off = effect absent (neutral). The sun's Affect atmospherics option has NO effect on it (docs, VRaySun page). Folded sub-toggle: Affect environment rays (doc default OFF — the VRaySky already accounts for scattered sunlight; enable only for artistic low-visibility looks, docs).
aerial.visibility_range — VRayAerialPerspective ▸ Parameters ▸ Visibility range (in meters) — kind:spinner unit:m range:[10,100000] default:10000 — Distance at which the haze has absorbed 90% of the light from objects behind it; lower = denser (docs). ALWAYS meters — converted internally from the current 3ds Max units (docs). Factory default not printed (10000 assumed; the docs' small demo scene uses 30-540 m).
aerial.atmosphere_height — VRayAerialPerspective ▸ Parameters ▸ Atmosphere height (in meters) — kind:spinner unit:m range:[10,100000] default:10000 — Height of the atmosphere layer in meters, converted internally from the scene units; lower values exaggerate the effect artistically and interact with scene scale (docs). Factory default not printed (10000 assumed). Practical range.
aerial.inscatter — VRayAerialPerspective ▸ Parameters ▸ Inscattered light intensity — kind:spinner unit:x range:[0,5] default:1 — Doc-stated default 1.0 = physically accurate amount of sunlight scattered into the haze; lower/higher only for artistic purposes (docs). Practical range; spinner bounds not stated in docs.
aerial.filter_color — VRayAerialPerspective ▸ Parameters ▸ Filter color — kind:color default:"white (no tint)" — Color swatch tinting the inscattered light (docs; their example shifts the hue of a red filter). white = untinted (derived neutral). Emit as an instruction, e.g. 'pale warm filter for golden-hour haze'.
aerial.affect_background — VRayAerialPerspective ▸ Parameters ▸ Affect background — kind:dropdown default:"on" — Options: on | off. Doc-stated default ON — the haze also covers camera rays that hit a background other than VRaySky; disabling gives cut-out looks (docs).

vantage33.label: Chaos Vantage 3.3

entries.ui_path: Environment tab ▸ Sky rollout ▸ Settings ▸ Environment mode
entries.notes: Options: Texture | Solid Color | Physical Sky. Physical Sky is available only when the imported .vrscene has a VRaySky texture (docs). Startup value follows the imported scene.

entries.ui_path: Environment tab ▸ Sky rollout ▸ Settings ▸ Load environment (Environment mode = Texture)
entries.notes: Loads the environment HDRI; RGB color space is deduced automatically (Auto) or set explicitly (docs). Value = HDRI file or mood description, not a number.

entries.ui_path: Environment tab ▸ Sky rollout ▸ Settings ▸ RGB color space
entries.notes: Options: sRGB | ACEScg | ... — color space the loaded environment texture is interpreted in. sRGB = default. Wrong color space skews the environment's color cast.

entries.ui_path: Environment tab ▸ Sky rollout ▸ Settings ▸ Flip horizontally
entries.notes: Mirrors the environment texture left-right. off = default. Use to flip the HDRI key-light to the other side.

entries.ui_path: Environment tab ▸ Sky rollout ▸ Settings ▸ Clamp to 1
entries.notes: Clamps environment values to 1.0, killing HDRI over-brights (and their strong key light). off = default (full HDR range). Leave off for physical lighting.

entries.ui_path: Environment tab ▸ Sky rollout ▸ Settings ▸ Rotation (Environment mode = Texture)
entries.notes: Rotation angle in degrees for the environment texture (docs) — use it to swing the HDRI key-light direction.

entries.ui_path: Environment tab ▸ Sky rollout ▸ Settings ▸ Intensity
entries.notes: Intensity of the environment lighting in every Environment mode (docs). 1.0 = neutral. Practical range; spinner bounds not stated in docs.

entries.ui_path: Environment tab ▸ Sky rollout ▸ Settings ▸ Sky model (Environment mode = Physical Sky)
entries.notes: Options: Preetham et al. | CIE Clear | CIE Overcast | Hosek et al. | PRG Clear Sky (old) | PRG Clear Sky. Updated PRG adds observer altitude, twilight to -12 deg and turbidity 1.81-4.89 (docs). Imported scenes keep their VRaySky model; default shown is the current model.

entries.ui_path: Environment tab ▸ Sun and Moon rollout ▸ Sun tab ▸ Enabled
entries.notes: Master on/off for Vantage's own sun. Imported V-Ray suns list in the Lights tab as Sun Light; Vantage's own sun is configured here (docs). on = default; state follows the scene.

entries.ui_path: Environment tab ▸ Sun and Moon rollout ▸ Sun tab ▸ [Sun Light] link
entries.notes: Links this sun to an imported Sun Light object so they stay in sync. off = default (independent). Linkage/plumbing — display-only, not a lighting value the model sets.

entries.ui_path: Environment tab ▸ Sun and Moon rollout ▸ Sun tab ▸ Intensity
entries.notes: Sun brightness multiplier. Default 0.033 confirmed from the UI capture (Vantage's default sun is a small fraction, tuned to its default exposure). Docs describe it as a way to reduce brightness; prefer exposure moves first. Practical range; UI accepts higher.

entries.ui_path: Environment tab ▸ Sun and Moon rollout ▸ Sun tab ▸ Sun size
entries.notes: Visible sun-disc size and shadow softness: lower = sharp shadows, higher = soft (docs). 1.0 = real sun. Practical range. On an imported Sun Light (Lights tab) the label is Sun size mult. (docs).

entries.ui_path: Environment tab ▸ Sun and Moon rollout ▸ Sun tab ▸ Color mode
entries.notes: Options: Filter | Direct | Override (docs). The Vantage sun has NO Kelvin control — warmth comes from Altitude + sky model, or Direct with a warm Color; numeric kelvin lives in post.wb_kelvin. Filter + white color = neutral/physical. Same control + options on an imported Sun Light (docs).

entries.ui_path: Environment tab ▸ Sun and Moon rollout ▸ Sun tab ▸ Sun position mode
entries.notes: Options: Manual | Altitude/Azimuth | Geolocation | Animated Geolocation (docs). Set Altitude/Azimuth so numeric recipe moves apply; scene default follows the import. On an imported Sun Light (Lights tab) the label is Sun position (docs).

entries.ui_path: Environment tab ▸ Sun and Moon rollout ▸ Sun tab ▸ Altitude (Sun position mode = Altitude/Azimuth)
entries.notes: Vantage names this control Altitude (this pack keys it sun.elevation): 0 = horizon, 90 = zenith; negative values give twilight (PRG sky renders the sun to -12 deg, docs). Default 45.0 confirmed from the UI capture. Same control on an imported Sun Light (docs).

entries.ui_path: Environment tab ▸ Sun and Moon rollout ▸ Sun tab ▸ Azimuth (Sun position mode = Altitude/Azimuth)
entries.notes: Compass azimuth from scene North, eastward — 90 = East (docs convention). Default 135.0 confirmed from the UI capture. Same control on an imported Sun Light (docs).

entries.ui_path: Environment tab ▸ Sun and Moon rollout ▸ Sun tab ▸ Invisible
entries.notes: Hides the sun disc from camera rays; it still lights the scene. off = default (disc visible). Turn on to keep a bright sun out of frame.

entries.ui_path: Camera tab ▸ Current camera options ▸ Resolution preset
entries.notes: Options: HD 1080 | UHD 4K | Custom | ... — a preset that fills width/height. Output framing only, not lighting — display-only.

entries.ui_path: Camera tab ▸ Current camera options ▸ Resolution (width × height)
entries.notes: Output resolution width×height. Framing/output only, not lighting — display-only.

entries.ui_path: Camera tab ▸ Current camera options ▸ Display:render ratio
entries.notes: Scales the viewport display resolution relative to render resolution. Display/perf only — display-only.

entries.ui_path: Camera tab ▸ Current camera options ▸ Camera type
entries.notes: Options: Standard | Spherical panorama | Cube 6x1 | ... — the projection model. Lens/projection, not lighting — display-only.

entries.ui_path: Camera tab ▸ Current camera options ▸ Lens mode
entries.notes: Options: Normal | Fisheye | ... — lens model. Lens geometry, not lighting — display-only.

entries.ui_path: Camera tab ▸ Current camera options ▸ Field of view
entries.notes: Horizontal field of view (deg). Framing/lens, not lighting — display-only.

entries.ui_path: Camera tab ▸ Current camera options ▸ Exposure (advanced) ▸ Exposure
entries.notes: Options: None | Physical | Value (docs). Physical uses ISO/F-Number/Shutter speed; Value uses Exposure Value and greys out ISO. Startup default not stated in current Chaos docs (Value assumed).

entries.ui_path: Camera tab ▸ Current camera options ▸ Exposure (advanced) ▸ Exposure Value (Exposure = Value)
entries.notes: Photographic EV: HIGHER = darker image. Sunny exterior lands around 14-15, interiors around 8-10; docs' twilight example uses EV 10. Factory default not stated in current Chaos docs (14 assumed).

entries.ui_path: Camera tab ▸ Current camera options ▸ Exposure (advanced) ▸ F-Number (Exposure = Physical)
entries.notes: Lens aperture; lower = brighter + more DOF. Active only when Exposure = Physical. Factory default not stated in current Chaos docs (8.0 assumed).

entries.ui_path: Camera tab ▸ Current camera options ▸ Vignetting
entries.notes: Plain lens vignetting darkening the frame corners. off = default. Docs recommend Optical vignetting (advanced DoF) instead. Lens artifact — display-only for lighting matches.

entries.ui_path: Camera tab ▸ Current camera options ▸ Motion blur (post)
entries.notes: Post-process motion blur. off = default. Motion/temporal, not lighting — display-only.

entries.ui_path: Camera tab ▸ Current camera options ▸ Depth of field (advanced: Focus distance, Aperture size, Optical vignetting)
entries.notes: Options: on | off. Keep DOF off for lighting matches unless the reference clearly shows it. Docs recommend Optical vignetting (advanced DoF) over the plain Vignetting toggle. Folded advanced sub-params: Focus distance, Aperture size, Center bias, Anisotropy, Blades, Optical vignetting — all lens/bokeh geometry, display-only.

entries.ui_path: Camera tab ▸ Current camera options ▸ Automatic vertical tilt correction
entries.notes: Two-point-perspective correction (with folded Tilt V/H and Shift V/H sub-params). off = default. Perspective geometry, not lighting — display-only.

entries.ui_path: Camera tab ▸ Current camera options ▸ Lens distortion
entries.notes: Barrel/pincushion lens distortion. 0 = none (default). Lens geometry, not lighting — display-only.

entries.ui_path: Camera tab ▸ Current camera options ▸ Camera clipping
entries.notes: Near/far clip planes. off = default. Visibility culling, not lighting — display-only.

entries.ui_path: Camera tab ▸ White balance (color swatch)
entries.notes: Color swatch — no Kelvin field on the camera; objects of the picked color render white (docs). Works only when Exposure = Physical or Value (docs). For numeric kelvin use post.wb_kelvin. Emit as an instruction, e.g. 'pick a pale warm tone to cool the image'.

entries.ui_path: Viewport bar ▸ Exposure ▸ Toggle auto-exposure
entries.notes: Options: on | off. When enabled it IGNORES the set camera exposure (docs) — it must be OFF for a recipe and between attempts, or EV moves do nothing. Startup state not stated in current Chaos docs (off recommended).

entries.ui_path: Color correction tab ▸ Exposure corrections (toggle)
entries.notes: Master toggle for Exposure bias / Highlight burn / Contrast below; viewport-wide post is also toggled via Viewport bar ▸ Toggle Color Corrections (docs). Neutral = off.

entries.ui_path: Color correction tab ▸ Exposure corrections ▸ Exposure bias
entries.notes: 0 = no change; the same control is exposed on the Viewport bar (docs). Practical range; slider bounds not stated in docs.

entries.ui_path: Color correction tab ▸ Exposure corrections ▸ Highlight burn
entries.notes: Applies exposure corrections to highlights; hidden while Filmic tonemap is on (docs). Range and neutral value follow the V-Ray burn convention (1.0 = no compression) — not stated in Vantage docs.

entries.ui_path: Color correction tab ▸ Exposure corrections ▸ Contrast
entries.notes: Positive pushes colors away from mid grey, negative toward it (docs); 0 = no change. Practical range; slider bounds not stated in docs.

entries.ui_path: Color correction tab ▸ Filmic tonemap (toggle)
entries.notes: Master toggle for the filmic tone curve; enabling it hides Highlight burn (docs). off = neutral (no filmic curve).

entries.ui_path: Color correction tab ▸ Filmic tonemap ▸ Type
entries.notes: Options: Hable | AMPAS (docs — Vantage exposes fewer curve types than the V-Ray VFB). Requires the Filmic tonemap toggle ON; enabling it hides Highlight burn (docs). Default selection not stated in current Chaos docs (Hable assumed).

entries.ui_path: Color correction tab ▸ Filmic tonemap ▸ Gamma
entries.notes: Output gamma of the filmic curve. 1.0 = default. Active with Filmic tonemap on.

entries.ui_path: Color correction tab ▸ Filmic tonemap ▸ Shoulder strength
entries.notes: Hable curve shoulder (highlight roll-off) strength. 0.15 = default. Higher softens highlights.
